requirements.requirement: Install AIDE and initialize a baseline database covering /etc on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed via dnf, the default /etc/aide.conf was confirmed to cover ~100 specific /etc paths plus a catch-all '/etc PERMS' rule, and `aide --init` produced a 28662-entry database in ~5s.

requirements.requirement: Activate the baseline database as the live reference and confirm it matches the current /etc state
requirements.summary: aide.db.new.gz was moved to the active aide.db.gz path, and a subsequent `aide --check` reported 'NO differences between database and filesystem', confirming the baseline is live and consistent.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate the baseline can identify and report later changes to /etc
requirements.summary: Appending a line to /etc/issue caused `aide --check` to exit 4 and report the exact changed file, size delta (23->47 bytes), and hash differences; reverting the file restored a clean check, directly proving the baseline's detect-and-report capability.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of the public contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (82d4f0d1...) and a clean AIDE db checksum were captured, `systemctl reboot` was issued with an immediate ack, connectivity was lost mid-reboot and then re-established, the post-restart boot_id (0659a87b...) differed confirming an actual reboot, and post-restart the AIDE db checksum was unchanged with `aide --check` again clean. This matches the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot showing the same new boot_id.

overall_summary: The executor established a functioning AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1: installed AIDE, initialized and activated a database covering /etc via the distro-default config, and directly proved detection capability by modifying and reverting /etc/issue with exact diff output. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated (boot_id change, db checksum and clean check preserved across reboot). All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, first-party evidence. The only shortcoming is minor operational hygiene: several temporary log/backup files were left in /tmp rather than cleaned up.
limitations: Minor /tmp residue (aide_check*.log, aide_init.log/pid, issue.orig, motd.orig, reboot.log) was left after task completion; low risk but not cleaned up.

No scheduled/cron integrity-check job (e.g. aidecheck.timer) was confirmed enabled; the task only required establishing the baseline, not automated periodic reporting, so this is not counted against the material outcomes but is worth noting as a scope boundary.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed executor commands chronologically: install/init/activate/verify of AIDE (cmd-3ff0c3f0d14e4859 through cmd-f6963127620c433f) are all directly required. cmd-5d6964a2ad594662 modified /etc/motd to test detection and was fully reverted by cmd-80749cf2a1204b90 (bounded, low-risk, restored). The /etc/issue mutation (cmd-1d32082301264bb9) and its revert (cmd-ea2478ff248d4617) are a reasonable, necessary proof of detection capability. The reboot (cmd-61b14f8ca0764080) is required by the independent restart protocol. The main hygiene issue is residue: /tmp/aide_check1.log through aide_check5.log, /tmp/aide_init.log, /tmp/aide_init.pid, /tmp/issue.orig, /tmp/motd.orig, and /tmp/reboot.log were left behind, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot versus before_prepare. These are low-risk, non-destructive scratch files in /tmp with no security or service impact, but were not cleaned up after task completion.
